name: Ancient world trivia (medium)
description: 50 medium questions about prehistory and the early civilizations: Mesopotamia, Egypt, the Indus, China, the Americas. Written by Claude from cited web pages; every question names its page. Checked by a second model pass; the questions it flagged were corrected or left out.

source.name: Web pages cited on each question

items.question: What was the main purpose of a Mesopotamian ziggurat?
answers: A temple dedicated to a city's patron god
A royal tomb for the city's kings
A fortress guarding the city's gates
A public granary for storing the harvest
items.correct: A temple dedicated to a city's patron god
items.explain: Ziggurats were tiered temple platforms for a city's patron deity. Unlike Egyptian pyramids, they were not royal burial places.

source.title: TC ziggurat in ancient Mesopotamia - Southern Cross University

items.question: Around 2100 BC, which ruler of Ur built ziggurats at Ur, Eridu, Uruk and Nippur?
items.explain: The Metropolitan Museum of Art notes that Ur-Nammu gained control of southern Mesopotamian cities around 2100 BC and built ziggurats in these cities.

source.title: Ur: The Ziggurat - The Metropolitan Museum of Art

items.question: The name of the Sumerian writing system, cuneiform, comes from a Latin word meaning what?
items.explain: Scribes pressed a reed into wet clay to make wedge-shaped marks. That gave the script its name, from the Latin for wedge.

source.title: These Sumerian inventions changed the world

items.question: In which museum is the famous stele inscribed with the Code of Hammurabi displayed today?
answers: The Metropolitan Museum of Art in New York
items.explain: A French expedition found the stele, and it has been in the Louvre since shortly after its discovery.

source.title: Code of Hammurabi: Ancient Babylonian Laws

items.question: The Code of Hammurabi stele was found in 1901 at which site in what is now Iran?
items.explain: A French team led by Jacques de Morgan found the stele at Susa. It had been carried there as war booty from Mesopotamia.

source.title: Code of Hammurabi: Ancient Babylonian Laws

items.question: According to the Epic of Gilgamesh, which Mesopotamian city did Gilgamesh rule as king?
items.explain: The epic presents Gilgamesh as the part-divine king of Uruk, a great builder and warrior.

source.title: Epic of Gilgamesh

items.question: In the Epic of Gilgamesh, which character is the wild man sent by the gods to temper the king's harsh rule?
items.explain: The god Anu had Enkidu created to check Gilgamesh's harsh rule. He then became the king's close friend.

source.title: Gilgamesh

items.question: In the Epic of Gilgamesh, what creature steals the plant that could renew Gilgamesh's youth?
items.explain: After Gilgamesh obtains the youth-renewing plant, a serpent seizes it. He returns to Uruk and accepts that he is mortal.

source.title: Epic of Gilgamesh

items.question: Around 2000 BC, which language mostly replaced Sumerian as a spoken language in Mesopotamia?
items.explain: Akkadian largely took over from Sumerian around 2000 BC. Sumerian survived for about 2,000 more years as a written language in cuneiform.

source.title: Sumer - Ancient, Map & Civilization

items.question: After the fall of the Akkadian Empire around 2150 BC, which people from the eastern highlands overran Sumer?
items.explain: National Geographic reports that Sumer was overrun by the Gutians, a people from the eastern highlands, after the Akkadian Empire fell.

source.title: These Sumerian inventions changed the world

items.question: On how many tablets does the fullest surviving version of the Epic of Gilgamesh appear?
items.explain: The fullest version of the epic is preserved on twelve incomplete tablets.

source.title: Gilgamesh

items.question: Which French scholar announced in September 1822 that he had deciphered Egyptian hieroglyphs using the Rosetta Stone?
items.explain: Champollion announced his decipherment on 27 September 1822. He matched the Greek text against the hieroglyphs on the stone.

source.title: Science history: Rosetta stone is deciphered, opening a window into ancient Egyptian civilization — Sept. 27, 1822

items.question: The Rosetta Stone carries a decree written in 196 BC during the reign of which king?
items.explain: The stone records a decree of Egyptian priests honoring Ptolemy V, written in 196 BC.

source.title: Champollion reveals decipherment of the Rosetta Stone

items.question: Which language, a descendant of ancient Egyptian, gave Champollion an advantage in cracking hieroglyphs?
items.explain: Champollion was fluent in Coptic, which descended from ancient Egyptian. This helped him match hieroglyphic signs to spoken sounds.

source.title: The Rosetta Stone: Discovery and Decoding Ancient Languages

items.question: For which pharaoh was the Great Pyramid of Giza built as a tomb?
items.explain: The Great Pyramid was the royal tomb of Khufu, also called Cheops, the second king of Egypt's 4th Dynasty.

source.title: Great Pyramid of Giza

items.question: What does archaeological evidence suggest about who built the Giza pyramids?
answers: Organized teams of free Egyptian laborers
items.correct: Organized teams of free Egyptian laborers
items.explain: Herodotus claimed Khufu enslaved his people, but archaeology points to free, professional builders.

source.title: What We Really Know About the Great Pyramid of Giza & Its Builder

items.question: The Great Pyramid was commissioned by Khufu, the son of which pharaoh?
items.explain: The Smithsonian describes the Great Pyramid as commissioned by Snefru's son Khufu.

source.title: The Egyptian Pyramid

items.question: Giza's three major pyramids were built for Khufu, his son Khafre, and which later king?
items.explain: The two other major Giza pyramids were built for Khafre and for a successor of Khafre, Menkaure.

source.title: The Egyptian Pyramid

items.question: Which wealthy English aristocrat financed Howard Carter's search for Tutankhamun's tomb?
items.explain: Carter's excavation was financed by the fifth Earl of Carnarvon, who nearly stopped funding it in 1922.

source.title: Howard Carter Opens King Tut's Tomb

items.question: How many coffins, nested inside a stone sarcophagus, held Tutankhamun's mummy?
items.explain: A stone sarcophagus held three coffins nested one inside another. The innermost was solid gold.

source.title: Entrance to King Tut's tomb discovered

items.question: About how old was Tutankhamun when he died?
items.explain: Tutankhamun, the 'boy king', died when he was about 18.

source.title: Entrance to King Tut's tomb discovered

items.question: What originally covered the outer surface of the Great Pyramid of Giza, giving it a gleaming look?
items.explain: The pyramid was clad in gleaming white limestone casing blocks. They were later stripped away, leaving the rougher core stones visible today.

source.title: Great Pyramid of Giza - World History Encyclopedia

items.question: At which Indus Valley city were the remains of the Great Bath found?
items.explain: The Great Bath was a large public water tank in the upper town of Mohenjo-daro, in present-day Pakistan.

source.title: Inside Mohenjo Daro, the 5,000-year-old metropolis frozen in time

items.question: Most Indus stamp seals were carved from which soft stone?
items.explain: Most Indus seals were small square pieces of steatite, a soft stone. They carried carved scenes and Indus script symbols.

source.title: Indus valley civilization - Students

items.question: The Indus civilization was first identified in 1921 at which site?
items.explain: Britannica says the civilization was identified at Harappa in 1921 and at Mohenjo-daro in 1922. That is why it is also called the Harappan civilization.

source.title: Indus civilization

items.question: Harappan seals and "colonies" point to extensive trade between the Indus civilization and which other region?
items.explain: Britannica describes Indus trade as extensive and well regulated. It arguably led to Harappan colonies in Mesopotamia.

source.title: Indus civilization

items.question: Roughly when did the Mature Harappan phase of the Indus civilization flourish?
items.explain: The Mature Harappan period is dated to about 2600–1900 BCE. During it the Indus script signs were somewhat standardized.

source.title: Indus script

items.question: Oracle bones bearing the earliest known Chinese writing come mainly from the Anyang capital of which dynasty?
items.explain: Oracle bones from Anyang, the Shang capital, carry the earliest known examples of Chinese writing.

source.title: 7 Everyday Objects From the Shang Dynasty

items.question: How did Shang diviners get an answer from an oracle bone?
answers: Tossing it like a die and reading how it landed
Burning incense beside it and reading the smoke
Applying heat until it cracked, then reading the cracks
Casting yarrow stalks over it and counting them
items.correct: Applying heat until it cracked, then reading the cracks
items.explain: The diviner presented a question with two possible outcomes, then applied heat to crack the bone or shell. The cracks were read as the answer.

source.title: 7 Everyday Objects From the Shang Dynasty

items.question: Besides cattle shoulder blades, which animal part was commonly inscribed for Shang divination?
items.explain: Oracle bones were made from cow scapulas and turtle shells.

source.title: 7 Everyday Objects From the Shang Dynasty

items.question: Before their importance was understood, inscribed bones dug up by farmers near Anyang were sold to be ground up for what use?
items.explain: For centuries farmers sold the inscribed fragments to apothecaries, who ground them up for traditional medicine.

source.title: 7 Everyday Objects From the Shang Dynasty

items.question: Anyang, site of the Shang capital Yinxu and its oracle bones, lies in which modern Chinese province?
items.explain: Systematic excavations at the Ruins of Yin (Yinxu) took place near Anyang in Henan Province.

source.title: Expedition Magazine

items.question: How were the warriors of the Terracotta Army first found in 1974?
items.explain: The tomb complex of China's first emperor was found by accident when farmers digging a well hit ceramic warrior figures.

source.title: The Tomb of the First Emperor

items.question: According to reports, roughly how many workers labored on Qin Shi Huang's tomb complex?
items.explain: Sources report that some 700,000 to 720,000 workers labored on the emperor's tomb complex.

source.title: What You Need to Know About China's Terra-Cotta Warriors and the First Qin Emperor

items.question: In what year BCE did Qin Shi Huang proclaim himself first emperor of China?
items.explain: Qin Shi Huang proclaimed himself first emperor of China in 221 BCE, after unifying the warring states.

source.title: What You Need to Know About China's Terra-Cotta Warriors and the First Qin Emperor

items.question: Whom do the Olmec colossal heads most likely portray?
items.explain: Britannica says the colossal heads are generally believed to be portraits of Olmec rulers.

source.title: Colossal head

items.question: After the decline of San Lorenzo, the Olmec center of power shifted to which site?
items.explain: The Olmecs were first centered at San Lorenzo Tenochtitlán. They moved to La Venta in the 10th century BC after San Lorenzo declined.

source.title: Olmecs

items.question: Caral, often described as the oldest city in the Americas, is located in which modern country?
items.explain: Caral lies in Peru's Supe Valley, about 200 km north of Lima. It is about 5,000 years old.

source.title: Caral

items.question: Which Peruvian archaeologist founded the archaeological project at Caral, working there from 1994 onward?
items.explain: Ruth Shady founded and directed the Caral project. She is credited with the discovery of the Norte Chico civilization.

source.title: Ruth Shady

items.question: In Maya numerals, which symbol stood for zero?
items.explain: Maya numbers used a dot for one, a bar for five and a shell glyph for zero.

source.title: Maya Calendar - Maya Archaeologist - Dr Diane Davies

items.question: The Maya number system was based on which number?
items.explain: Maya numerals were vigesimal, meaning base 20.

source.title: Maya numerals

items.question: How many days made up the Maya sacred calendar, the Tzolk'in?
items.explain: The Tzolk'in combined a cycle of 20 day names with 13 numbers, giving 260 days. The 365-day count was a separate solar calendar.

source.title: The Maya Calendar Explained - Maya Archaeologist - Dr Diane Davies

items.question: In the Maya Lowlands, Tikal's great rival for power was which city?
items.explain: In the Maya Lowlands, the cities of Tikal and Calakmul became two great rivals for power.

source.title: Maya civilization

items.question: Göbekli Tepe's monumental stone enclosures in Turkey were built by what kind of people?
answers: Early farmers growing wheat and barley
Hunter-gatherers who had not yet farmed
items.correct: Hunter-gatherers who had not yet farmed
items.explain: Göbekli Tepe's builders were hunter-gatherers living around the start of the Neolithic. They built the monuments before farming was established.

source.title: Features - Last Stand of the Hunter-Gatherers? - Archaeology Magazine - May/June 2021

items.question: What does the Turkish name Göbekli Tepe mean?
items.explain: Local farmers called the site Göbekli Tepe, meaning 'Potbelly Hill'.

source.title: Why Göbekli Tepe Changed Everything About Prehistory

items.question: The Lascaux cave in France contains about 600 paintings and roughly how many engravings?
items.explain: Britannica says Lascaux holds approximately 600 paintings and 1,500 engravings.

source.title: Lascaux

items.question: Who stumbled upon the Lascaux cave paintings in 1940?
answers: A shepherd searching for a lost goat
Teenagers who followed a dog into the cave
items.correct: Teenagers who followed a dog into the cave
items.explain: Four teenagers found the cave near Montignac after following their dog down a narrow entrance.

source.title: Lascaux cave paintings discovered

items.question: About how old are the paintings in the Lascaux cave in France?
items.explain: The Lascaux paintings are approximately 17,000 years old, from the Upper Paleolithic.

source.title: Lascaux

items.question: Which Spanish cave's paintings, found in 1879, were at first widely doubted as authentic?
items.explain: The first Upper Paleolithic cave paintings were found at Altamira in 1879 by a landowner, Marcelino Sanz de Sautuola. Many doubted they were genuine.

source.title: Lascaux Cave Paintings

items.question: Which archaeologist coined the term "Neolithic Revolution" for the shift from hunting and gathering to farming?
items.explain: Gordon Childe called the shift to farming and settled life the 'Neolithic Revolution'. For decades this was the standard model of early human development.

source.title: Why Göbekli Tepe Changed Everything About Prehistory
